source.title: A Modern Take on the Bias-Variance Tradeoff in Neural Networks
source.authors: Brady Neal; Sarthak Mittal; A. Baratin; Vinayak Tantia; M. Scicluna; Simon Lacoste-Julien; Ioannis Mitliagkas

record.tranche_reason: The study varies neural-network size and measures test error, directly testing the size-wise error trend in different settings. Its experiments are not an explicit replication of the cited double-descent study.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test-error results for width and depth sweeps. Most values are plotted rather than stated numerically; figure-only values are recorded as such. Double-descent findings cited from other work are not rows. The paper does not test test error over epochs or sample size.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps hidden-layer width (and, separately, depth) in fully connected networks and plots 0-1 test error, so its own results bear on model-wise double descent (V1). Its aim is bias and variance, not double descent. It never locates the interpolation threshold and uses no label noise.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors find that both bias and variance decrease with network width, against Geman et al.'s tradeoff claim. Optimization variance falls with width and sampling variance plateaus; linear-model theory is consistent with this. Training-time dynamics are left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps neural-network width and measures test error, but focuses on bias and variance in fully connected single-hidden-layer networks and does not identify a peak at the interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: On small-data MNIST, the test-error curve differs between per-width tuned learning rates and a fixed step size of 0.01. The depth results also vary across vanilla networks, skip connections, and dynamical isometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Variance falls with width. Variance due to optimization falls with width, while variance due to sampling rises slowly and plateaus once the network is over-parameterized.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In over-parameterized networks, prediction variance decreases with width, driven by vanishing optimization variance.

record.problems: Test-error values are mostly available only in plots, with no stated uncertainty for those measurements. The width experiments do not explicitly locate the interpolation threshold or test the peak's position relative to it. Learning-rate choice changes the small-data result.
record.rows_left_out: None of the study's other plots were left out that report test error against model size; bias and variance measurements and the linear-model variance derivations were omitted because they do not measure the test-error shapes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Location of any peak relative to a measured interpolation threshold; behaviour under label noise; convolutional or residual architectures.
All; the authors did not study changes over training.
All; the linear-model theory concerns variance only, not a risk curve across model classes.
All; no label-noise or regularization sweeps.

missing.what: Test error vs width on small MNIST with batch gradient descent (Fig. 13) and LBFGS (Fig. 14); both show decreasing error. rows_left_out wrongly says no test-error-vs-size plots were omitted.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tranche of T1 is overstated: the study is not a double-descent replication and never identifies the interpolation threshold. Its widths likely span the full-MNIST threshold, but the paper does not say so. The width-sweep challenge is therefore weak and should be read alongside V6, since the original peak is strongest with label noise.

versions.untested_parts: Tests width and depth sweeps in fully connected networks, but does not locate a double-descent peak relative to a measured interpolation threshold.
The paper states that it did not study how bias and variance change over training; it does not report an epoch-wise test-error sweep.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold is reported.
The empirical size sweeps use neural networks; the linear-model theory concerns variance, not a general risk curve across model classes.
The paper discusses effective capacity but does not test whether one measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
No systematic test of label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization is reported.
The study does not replot risk against an effective parameter count or test whether that changes the curve shape.

rows.subject: fully connected single hidden layer neural networks
rows.size_stated: hidden-unit widths varied; exact values not stated in text
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-layer width and plotted test error with a fixed step size.
rows.note: The authors describe a U-shaped test-error curve in this fixed-step-size setting, attributing it to the step size being good for some network sizes and bad for others; it does not show the full claimed fall-rise-fall pattern.
rows.check: Text attributes the Fig. 12 'U curve' to a step size that is good for some widths and bad for others. It is unclear whether the U refers to test error or to bias/variance, and there is no fall-rise-fall reading. This is a learning-rate control, not evidence on the peak.

rows.subject: vanilla fully connected networks
rows.stage_stated: all networks had training error 0 and were trained to training loss 5e-5
rows.operation_detail: Varied network depth and plotted test error.
rows.note: The authors say test error quickly degrades with depth and the bias curve is not monotone; they do not report a second descent.
rows.check: All depths already have training error 0, so the sweep lies entirely past interpolation. Test error 'quickly degrades' with depth, the opposite of the second descent. The authors flag training confounds.

relationships.condition: Width sweeps of single-hidden-layer FC nets on MNIST, CIFAR10 (with and without early stopping), SVHN, small MNIST (tuned step size, SGD/GD/LBFGS) and sinusoid regression; no added label noise.
relationships.reason: Authors describe test error as decreasing with width, tracking decreasing bias and variance, with no peak reported (R1-R5, R7). Caveat: the threshold is not located and the setting has no label noise, so a narrow or noise-dependent peak may be unresolved.
relationships.display_finding: Across classification experiments and noisy sinusoid regression, test error decreased with width alongside bias and variance, without a reported peak; interpolation thresholds were not located.

relationships.condition: Depth sweeps of FC nets, all at zero training error (vanilla, skip connections, dynamical isometry).
relationships.reason: Past interpolation, adding depth raises test error (R8, R9) or leaves it flat at about +0.1% (R10). The post-threshold improvement does not extend to depth here, though the authors note training confounds.
relationships.display_finding: Additional depth increased test error or left it nearly unchanged, with about a +0.1% change under dynamical isometry, although training confounds complicated interpretation.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Depth sweeps of FC nets, all at zero training error (vanilla, skip connections, dynamical isometry).
source_check.reason: Figures 21–23 establish worsening or nearly unchanged test error as depth increases among interpolating networks. This qualifies extending post-interpolation improvement to depth; it does not establish the full threshold-crossing curve, and Appendix C.2 identifies training confounds.
